events.name: Greenville County Republican Party Quarterly Meeting
events.event: The county party's regular quarterly meeting, with local, state and federal candidates appearing.
events.location: Greenville Tech Campus, Multipurpose Room in the Prisma Health Center building, Greenville
events.notes: Doors open at 5:30 pm and the meeting starts at 6:30 pm, running to 8:30 pm. This is a partisan organisation's own meeting. Check the party's notice before setting out.

events.name: SC Governor Debate
events.event: Alan Wilson (R) and Jermaine Johnson (D) meet in the televised debate for the governor of South Carolina.
events.notes: Runs 7:00 pm to 8:00 pm and is streamed live by WIS. Whether the studio admits an audience has not been published, so treat that as unknown rather than settled either way.

events.name: SC-04 Congressional Debate
events.event: William Timmons (R), the incumbent, and Courtney McClain (D) meet in the televised debate for South Carolina's 4th Congressional District.
events.notes: Runs 7:00 pm to 8:00 pm and is broadcast by FOX Carolina. SC-04 covers the Greenville area, so this is the Upstate's own congressional race.

events.name: SCETV U.S. Senate Debate
events.event: Dr. Annie Andrews (D), Sen. Darline Graham (R) and Dr. Kasie Whitener (L) meet in the televised debate for the United States Senate seat, streamed from Columbia by SCETV.
events.notes: SCETV published the 7:00 pm start on 25 September. It is broadcast and streamed live across SCETV's television and radio networks. Three candidates are confirmed participants, not two.

events.name: Early Voting (in person)
events.event: In-person early voting runs for two weeks at early voting centers across South Carolina. Polls are open 8:30 am to 6:00 pm, and closed on Sunday 25 October.
events.location: Early voting centers in your county, statewide
events.notes: You may use any early voting center in your county, not only the one nearest your home. Check scvotes.gov, or your county's election office, before travelling.

events.name: General Election
events.event: South Carolina votes for a United States senator, the governor, all seven House of Representatives seats, the state House of Representatives and county offices. Upstate voters also decide SC-04 between William Timmons and Courtney McClain, and SC-03, where Sheri Biggs is the candidate.
events.notes: Polls are open 7:00 am until 7:00 pm. Confirm your polling place with your county election office before you go. If you are in line when the polls close, you are entitled to vote.

events.name: City of Greenwood General Election
events.event: Greenwood holds its own general election on the same day as the state and federal vote, for city offices and any municipal contests on the ballot.
events.notes: Held on the same day as the state and federal election. Greenwood is the county seat of Greenwood County. Confirm your polling place with Greenwood County.

pageNote.heading: Ongoing campaign activity in the Upstate
paragraphs: Darline Graham (U.S. Senate) has been making repeated stops in the Upstate, most recently a meet-and-greet luncheon at the Poinsett Club in Greenville on 21 September, hosted by the Upstate Republican Women's Club.
Annie Andrews (D) has also held events in the Upstate and pressed for televised debates in the region. Both campaigns have agreed to the SCETV debate on 11 October.
Alan Wilson (R, Governor) campaigned in Greenville and Laurens counties during the primary.
William Timmons (R, SC-04) is the incumbent in the Upstate congressional seat and is contesting it against Courtney McClain. They debate on 8 October.
Sheri Biggs (R, SC-03) covers the Anderson and Greenwood area and is running for re-election.
